description:
Source guards fail when a second repository publication path appears, retargeted from the kernel they name today.

## Background

A scratch-built suite carries source-text guards over the workspace: no raw filesystem writes in the command layer, no predecessor or compatibility module, one canonical renderer owner, one package-tree publisher, and a capture that addresses no source by pathname. Its header names the kernel module as the compiler-enforced half of the guarantee, and several guards name the kernel and the atomic-write module directly.

With the kernel gone, the guards retarget onto what carries the property: the redo record is the one mechanism that writes repository state, and the initialization root publisher is its single named exception.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A guard fails when a module other than the redo record and the initialization root publisher writes repository state directly.
- [hard] REQ-02: The named exception for creating an absent data root is stated once, in the guard, with its reason.
- [hard] REQ-03: Guards naming the retired kernel modules are retargeted, with the reason stated where each lands.
- [hard] REQ-04: The suite adds no new integration-test target.
- [hard] REQ-05: The guards assert a semantic property rather than a copied inventory of file names.
title: Publication path source guards
